editorial:
Ever wondered what happens when a lonely astronaut loses his mind in the middle of nowhere? You get a wild ride with Astronaut Williams, a guy who is convinced there is a creature called the Space Wolf hiding in the dark corners of the galaxy. The vibe is super quirky and a bit weird, blending a small-scale drama with some really strange sci-fi ideas. It feels like a passion project that does not take itself too seriously, making you feel like you are in on a big secret while watching Williams struggle with his own reality.

What really works here is the lead performance, which keeps you guessing if the monster is real or just in his head. The pacing is a bit slow at times, but the weird twists make up for it. If you love odd indie films that feel like a fever dream, you should definitely give this a shot.
endingExplained: At the very end, you find out that the Space Wolf was never a physical monster. It was actually a way for Williams to deal with his loneliness and grief while floating in space. He finally accepts his situation and stops fighting the imaginary beast. The movie wraps up with him finding peace, showing that the real battle was always happening inside his own mind rather than in the stars.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky indie sci-fi and character studies.
